html:
A system of dams, tunnels and power stations built in the Snowy Mountains of southeast Australia between 1949 and 1974. It is the largest engineering project ever undertaken in the country.

The scheme turns the Snowy River and its neighbours inland. Water that once ran south to the sea now passes through tunnels under the mountains, makes electricity on the way down, and flows into the Murray and Murrumbidgee rivers to irrigate farms. It has sixteen major dams, nine power stations and about 225 kilometres of tunnels, pipelines and aqueducts.

Prime Minister Ben Chifley launched it in 1949, and engineer William Hudson ran it for twenty years. More than 100,000 people worked on it, most of them migrants from over thirty countries who came in the wave of postwar migration. The scheme became a symbol of the new multicultural Australia. More than a hundred workers died.

The project was finished on time and on budget. Its cost came later to the Snowy River itself, which shrank to a trickle until some flow was restored in the 2000s.
sum: A system of dams, tunnels and power stations built in the Snowy Mountains of southeast Australia between 1949 and 1974. It is the largest engineering project ever undertaken in the country.
